full_text_en:
Case of Acquittal of Wang Lisheng

Defendant: Wang Lisheng, male, 50 years old, chief engineer of Zhejiang Light and Textile Industry Design Institute, arrested on July 16, 1991, and released on bail pending trial on April 14, 1992.

The case of Wang Lisheng for corruption was initiated by the Xiacheng District People's Procuratorate of Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, which instituted a public prosecution before the Xiacheng District People's Court.

The prosecution alleged: In August 1988, while representing Zhejiang Light and Textile Industry Design Institute (hereinafter referred to as the Provincial Design Institute) in negotiations to sign a contract for the provision of technical services with Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant in Jiangsu Province, the defendant took advantage of his position to demand RMB 15,000 in technical service fees from the other party, to be paid by both check and cash. After the other party agreed, Wang Lisheng deceived the leadership of the Provincial Design Institute by stating that the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant would only pay RMB 1,000 in technical service fees. After the technical services were completed, in accordance with Wang Lisheng’s instructions, the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant remitted RMB 1,000 to the Provincial Design Institute, and the remaining RMB 14,000 was collected by Wang Lisheng under the name of the Hangzhou Textile Industry Design Office (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Design Office). Wang Lisheng distributed RMB 4,000 of that amount to the Municipal Design Office as compensation, and he personally obtained RMB 10,000, thereby constituting the crime of corruption.

After a public trial, the Xiacheng District People’s Court, in addition to confirming the facts alleged in the prosecution, also found that: out of the RMB 10,000 obtained by the defendant Wang Lisheng, he paid RMB 1,200 to relevant personnel of the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant, and he personally obtained RMB 8,800. In October 1990, Wang Lisheng falsely told the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant that the leadership did not dare to assume responsibility and that the funds could not be distributed. He then returned the RMB 8,800 along with personal funds to make up RMB 10,000, and requested that the plant remit the amount by check to the Municipal Design Office. After receiving the funds, the Municipal Design Office gave Wang Lisheng RMB 300 under the heading of business expenses.

The Xiacheng District People’s Court held: As a state functionary, Wang Lisheng took advantage of the convenience provided by his unit’s assignment of technical services to deceive the unit’s leadership and appropriate part of public funds for himself. However, considering that Wang Lisheng had fully returned the funds before the case was filed and investigated, his conduct was of a clearly minor nature, caused little harm, and thus did not constitute a crime. The Municipal Design Office, which did not participate in the technical services, received RMB 14,000, which constituted unjust enrichment. Accordingly, on May 5, 1992, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The defendant Wang Lisheng is declared not guilty. 2. The RMB 14,000 transferred with the case is to be confiscated by law and turned over to the State Treasury.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the Xiacheng District People’s Procuratorate of Hangzhou, believing that the judgment was clearly erroneous, filed a protest with the Hangzhou Intermediate People’s Court. The grounds were: 1. Out of the RMB 15,000 demanded by Wang Lisheng from the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant, except for RMB 1,000 directly remitted to the Provincial Design Institute and RMB 4,000 paid by Wang Lisheng as compensation to the Municipal Design Office, the remaining RMB 10,000 was all received and retained by Wang Lisheng himself, not RMB 8,800, and his conduct constituted the crime of corruption. Only after his corrupt acts were exposed, in order to conceal his crimes and resist investigation, did Wang Lisheng transfer the RMB 10,000 to the Municipal Design Office; this is different from voluntarily returning illicit gains before the case was filed and investigated. It is a matter of attitude after the crime, affecting only the sentencing of Wang Lisheng, not the characterization of his conduct. The judgment of first instance, which declared him not guilty on the grounds that his attitude after the crime rendered his conduct of a clearly minor nature and caused little harm, was erroneous. 2. Wang Lisheng was dispatched by the Provincial Design Institute to complete the design tasks for the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant. The ownership of the RMB 15,000 in remuneration should belong to the Provincial Design Institute, but RMB 14,000 was intercepted by Wang Lisheng. It was also incorrect to treat the RMB 14,000 as unjust enrichment of the Municipal Design Office and to confiscate it for the State Treasury.

The Hangzhou Intermediate People’s Court conducted a public trial of this case and found:

The defendant Wang Lisheng had previously successfully led the design work of monomer recovery units on several occasions. In early 1988, the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant in Jiangsu Province intended to build a monomer recovery unit to treat wastewater and recover usable substances from the wastewater. It dispatched engineer Wang Youfu, who was in charge of this work, to inspect facilities in Shanghai, Beijing, and elsewhere. It was learned that building such a unit, excluding civil construction costs, would require an investment of approximately RMB 2 million, with high energy consumption, which the plant could hardly bear. In August of that year, through an introduction, Wang Youfu went to Hangzhou to inspect a monomer recovery unit designed under Wang Lisheng’s leadership, which required only an investment of RMB 700,000, with low energy consumption and good benefits. He then reported to the leadership and decided to invite Wang Lisheng to undertake the design. While discussing this matter with Wang Lisheng on behalf of the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant, Wang Youfu was told by Wang Lisheng that a technical service fee of RMB 15,000 was required, and that Wang Lisheng wanted a larger personal share and a smaller share for the unit. The Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant agreed but requested that cash be collected through the unit’s formal procedures. On August 10, Wang Lisheng contacted Xin Zuoyou, the head of the Municipal Design Office, and claimed that he had undertaken the design work for the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant. To facilitate the collection of cash, he requested Xin Zuoyou’s assistance in signing the agreement and handling the settlement procedures under the name of the Municipal Design Office, from which the office could receive compensation. Xin Zuoyou agreed. Considering that completing this design task would require not only some working hours but also an on-site inspection of the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant, Wang Lisheng drafted the agreement to read: The Municipal Design Office is generally responsible for the engineering technical consultation and design of the monomer recovery unit of the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant (part of the process to be coordinated with the Provincial Design Institute), with a total fee of RMB 15,000, to be paid by both cash and check (the fee of RMB 1,000 for the Provincial Design Institute to be directly remitted by the plant to the institute’s account, deducted from the RMB 15,000). After drafting the agreement, Xin Zuoyou affixed the official seal of the Municipal Design Office and noted the bank account number. Wang Lisheng also drafted five cash receipts of RMB 2,000 each in the name of the Municipal Design Office, and Xin Zuoyou again affixed the official seal. On August 13, Wang Lisheng reported to the leadership of the Provincial Design Institute that the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant had requested the design of a monomer recovery unit, but falsely stated that only existing drawings needed to be copied, requiring no further work, and that the other party would pay only RMB 1,000. After obtaining the leadership’s consent, Wang Lisheng filled out a contract form under the name of the Provincial Design Institute’s Staff Technical Association, which was sealed by the unit. On August 16, Wang Lisheng brought the agreement and contract to the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant. The plant found the terms of the agreement and contract feasible and affixed its official seal. Thereafter, Wang Lisheng, primarily using his spare time, designed 11 drawings for the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant. Jiang Futian of the Provincial Design Institute designed one drawing. All drawings were traced by Wang Lisheng’s daughter and then reviewed by Luo Qiongtian of the Provincial Design Institute. Based on these drawings, the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant constructed the monomer recovery unit, which was successfully commissioned on the first attempt. From the time the unit went into operation until the time of the investigation by the court of second instance, it had created economic benefits of RMB 1.3 million, while also reducing environmental pollution from wastewater. In accordance with the agreement, the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant remitted RMB 4,000 by check to the Municipal Design Office and RMB 1,000 to the Provincial Design Institute. Additionally, as the project progressed, it allowed Wang Lisheng to collect RMB 10,000 in cash in four installments using the Municipal Design Office’s receipts. After receiving the cash, Wang Lisheng distributed RMB 1,200 to personnel of the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant who participated in the construction of the monomer recovery unit, under the heading of bonuses.

In August 1990, while investigating another case, the Huzhou City People’s Procuratorate of Zhejiang Province suspected that Wang Lisheng might have been involved in bribery in that case. Upon learning of this, Wang Lisheng became concerned about the cash he had received from the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant and handed the RMB 10,000 to Xin Zuoyou. Xin Zuoyou said, “You should distribute this money as you see fit; if you think there is a problem, just send it back to the plant.” Wang Lisheng then had his wife send the RMB 10,000 to the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant in the name of the Municipal Design Office. The plant remitted the amount by check to the Municipal Design Office. In July 1991, the Xiacheng District People’s Procuratorate filed and investigated this case.

The above facts are confirmed by documentary evidence and witness testimony. The facts are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient.

The Hangzhou Intermediate People’s Court held: (1) Wang Lisheng’s conduct did not have the social harmfulness required under the Criminal Law. According to Article 10 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, the key to determining whether an act constitutes a crime is whether it is socially harmful. The defendant Wang Lisheng, relying on his professional technical skills and primarily using his spare time, undertook the overall design task of the monomer recovery unit for the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant. After the plant adopted his design, it saved investment, achieved success on the first commissioning, and obtained significant economic benefits. Wang Lisheng’s conduct not only lacked the social harmfulness necessary for a crime but also made a beneficial contribution to society; therefore, it cannot be treated as a crime. (2) Wang Lisheng’s conduct did not conform to the essential characteristics of the crime of corruption. According to Article 155 of the Criminal Law and Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on Punishing Crimes of Corruption and Bribery, the crime of corruption refers to the offense of a person engaged in public service according to law, who uses his position to violate public property. Wang Lisheng did not initially accept a commission from his unit to undertake the design work of the monomer recovery unit for the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant. Instead, after negotiating the terms for providing design services with the plant in his personal capacity, he used the names of the Municipal Design Office and the Provincial Design Institute to sign the agreement with the plant, in order to meet the plant’s requirement that payment be made through the unit’s formal procedures and to facilitate future withdrawal of service fees. This conduct should not be regarded as Wang Lisheng being commissioned by his unit to engage in public service. Moreover, the design task was primarily completed by Wang Lisheng using his spare time, and in terms of process and pipeline design, it differed from the application of basic principles of monomer recovery units he had previously designed. Therefore, under his agreement with the chemical fertilizer plant, he was entitled to receive corresponding remuneration, consistent with the provision in the March 1985 Decision on the Reform of the Science and Technology System that “scientific and technical personnel may, on the premise of completing their regular work and not infringing upon the technical rights and economic interests of their units, engage in spare-time technical work and consulting services, and the income belongs to themselves.” The RMB 10,000 cash collected by Wang Lisheng, except for the portion to be distributed to others who participated in the design, was his own remuneration and did not belong to public property. Therefore, Wang Lisheng’s conduct did not involve using his position to unlawfully possess public property with intent, and did not conform to the essential characteristics of the crime of corruption. (3) Some of Wang Lisheng’s practices in undertaking the design and receiving remuneration were improper. These are matters for criticism and education and cannot be punished under the Criminal Law.

In summary, the conduct of the defendant Wang Lisheng did not constitute the crime of corruption. The protest and the judgment of first instance, which only considered the superficial phenomenon of Wang Lisheng deceiving the unit’s leadership, concluded that Wang Lisheng was commissioned to engage in public service, and then reached the erroneous conclusions that “the RMB 15,000 was public funds” and “Wang Lisheng appropriated public funds.” Although the judgment of first instance declared Wang Lisheng not guilty, the grounds for acquittal were improper and should be corrected.

Although the overall design work of the monomer recovery unit of the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant was primarily completed by the defendant Wang Lisheng in his spare time, it also occupied some working hours and involved the labor of others in the Provincial Design Institute. Therefore, the compensation paid by the Yangzhou Chemical Fertilizer Plant should be distributed by the Provincial Design Institute in accordance with the relevant regulations on scientific and technical personnel engaging in spare-time part-time technical services. The Municipal Design Office, which did not participate in the design work, received RMB 4,000 from Wang Lisheng solely for lending its official seal and bank account; this amount is illegal income and should be recovered. In declaring Wang Lisheng not guilty, the judgment of first instance also confiscated and turned over to the State Treasury the entire RMB 14,000, including Wang Lisheng’s labor remuneration, which was manifestly inappropriate and should be amended. The protest grounds of the Xiacheng District People’s Procuratorate of Hangzhou are inconsistent with the facts of this case and are not adopted. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 136, Item (3) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, the Hangzhou Intermediate People’s Court rendered the following final judgment on August 20, 1992:

1. Item 1 of the judgment of first instance is affirmed, and Item 2 is reversed.

2. Of the RMB 14,000 transferred with the case, RMB 4,000 constitutes illegal income of the Municipal Design Office and shall be recovered and turned over to the State Treasury.
